claims.text: The initial nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and form a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
The balance between configurational entropy and thermally activated atomic diffusion governs the stability of equiatomic multimetal nanoparticles.
Sufficiently rapid temperature-driven diffusion can override entropy-driven stabilization and trigger phase segregation.
Oxidizing conditions compound diffusion-driven instability and can trigger oxidation.
Materials with intrinsically higher diffusion barriers remain stable solid solutions over a wider high-temperature operating range.
In situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction can detect time- and temperature-dependent phase formation or transformation.
Comparing inert or reducing and oxidizing atmospheres distinguishes diffusion-only effects from effects compounded by oxidation.
Diffraction changes and elemental mapping can reveal the onset of phase segregation or oxide-domain formation.
At lower temperatures, configurational entropy suppresses phase separation and maintains a uniform solid solution.
Increasing temperature enables atoms to overcome diffusion barriers.
Lower diffusion activation energies produce greater atomic diffusion and thereby promote segregation into distinct phases.
Oxidation can drive element-specific migration and chemical depletion of the parent alloy.
Refractory-metal constituents have higher diffusion barriers that delay or suppress diffusion-driven segregation and oxidation.
Refractory-containing nanoparticles will retain a single-phase structure and chemical homogeneity to higher temperatures than nanoparticles containing more mobile elements.
Nanoparticles with lower diffusion barriers will exhibit phase separation or surface oxidation at lower temperatures relative to their initial homogeneous state.
Atomic diffusion is minimal at ambient or low operating temperature in the proposed baseline state.
The onset of observable segregation or oxidation depends on both temperature and environmental oxygen partial pressure.
The transition temperature varies with elemental composition and constituent diffusion barriers.
